readmeExcerpt: Qrisp is a high-level quantum programming framework that allows for intuitive development of quantum algorithms. It provides a rich set of tools and abstractions to make quantum computing more accessible to developers and researchers. By automating many steps one usually encounters when programming a quantum computer, introducing quantum types, and many more features Qrisp makes quantum programming more user-friendly yet stays performant when it comes to compiling programs to the circuit level. quickstart.source:
from qrisp import QuantumFloat, QuantumModulus, h, QFT, control

def find_order(a, N):
    qg = QuantumModulus(N)
    qg[:] = 1
    qpe_res = QuantumFloat(2*qg.size + 1, exponent = -(2*qg.size + 1))
    h(qpe_res)
    for i in range(len(qpe_res)):
        with control(qpe_res[i]):
            qg *= a
        a = (a*a)%N
    QFT(qpe_res, inv = True)
    return qpe_res.get_measurement()
